source.title: Introduction to the Yang-Baxter Equation with Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Classify all solutions of the Yang-Baxter equation in the braid-relation form: for a vector space V over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, determine all linear automorphisms R of V tensor V satisfying (R tensor id) o (id tensor R) o (R tensor id) = (id tensor R) o (R tensor id) o (id tensor R) as automorphisms of V tensor V tensor V.

evidence.quote: Finding all solutions of the Yang-Baxter equation is a difficult task far from being resolved.
However, the full classification of its solutions remains an open problem.

accepted.question_text: For Yang-Baxter operators obtained from algebra structures, can these operators be obtained from a universal R-matrix, with the universal R-matrix understood in connection with quasi-triangular structures? Here a Yang-Baxter operator is an invertible solution of the Yang-Baxter braid relation, and the algebra-structure family refers to operators arising from k-algebras.

evidence.quote: Conjecture. The YB operators from algebra structures can be obtained from some kind of universal R-matrix
Such an operator is called a Yang-Baxter operator, or, simply, a YB operator.

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest dimension of a finite-dimensional vector space over the algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k for which there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators. A Yang-Baxter operator is an invertible solution of the Yang-Baxter braid relation, and the motivating existence result asserts only that some finite-dimensional vector spaces have infinitely many non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal dimension for infinitely many YB operators

evidence.quote: Theorem 2. There exist finite dimensional vector spaces for which there are infinitely many non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators.
Some directions for future research are: Finding the smallest dimension of a vector space for which Theorem 2 holds

trace.notes: Normalized one URL source. Direct fetch of https://zbmath.org/6330786 returned a Cloudflare challenge, so the zbMATH REST API was used only as resolver metadata. The API identified DOI 10.3390/axioms1010033 and title Introduction to the Yang-Baxter equation with open problems. The DOI resolved to the MDPI article page; local PDF download from MDPI failed due DNS resolution for www.mdpi.com, so the MDPI full-text HTML page was used for extraction.

Mapped the article structure: Abstract; 1. Introduction; 2. Preliminaries; 3. Main Results and Discussion; 4. Conclusions and Directions for Future Research; Acknowledgments; References and Notes. Key definitions include the Yang-Baxter equation, the set-theoretical Yang-Baxter equation, relation-derived maps, Yang-Baxter operators, and isomorphism of YB operators. Likely open-problem regions were the introduction, preliminaries, main-results conjecture, and future-research section.
Extracted the broad open problem that the full classification, or equivalently finding all solutions, of the Yang-Baxter equation remains unresolved.
Extracted the explicitly labeled conjecture about obtaining YB operators from algebra structures from a universal R-matrix.
Extracted two future-research directions: finding the smallest dimension for Theorem 2 and studying relation-derived solutions for other nonlinear equations in quantum group theory.

Expanded the compressed classification statement using the article's preliminary setup: V over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and R satisfying the braid-relation version of the Yang-Baxter equation.
Expanded the conjecture by inlining that a YB operator is an invertible solution of the Yang-Baxter equation and preserving the source's universal R-matrix and quasi-triangular-structure context.
